thesis: Adobe is the inverse of everything else we have analyzed this week: a wide-moat software franchise whose stock fell 30-37% in 2026 on an AI-disruption narrative (intensified by Anthropic's Claude Design launch in April and generative rivals like Midjourney/Sora/Canva) while its actual results accelerated - Q2 FY2026 revenue $6.62B (+12.7%, a beat), FY2026 guidance RAISED to $26.5-26.6B, ARR +10.2%, and a 13.15% FCF yield (P/FCF ~10, forward P/E ~9). The market is pricing terminal decline; the reported numbers show a growing business. That gap - if the disruption is slower or shallower than feared - is the largest positive margin of safety we have found.
catalysts: Q3 FY2026 results (~September 2026): guidance $6.67-6.72B - a third consecutive beat-and-raise would crack the decline narrative
Firefly/AI monetization metrics (AI-influenced ARR disclosures) - the direct rebuttal to the disruption thesis
Buyback math: at a 13% FCF yield, repurchases retire ~10%+ of shares annually at these prices
CEO transition resolution (uncertainty currently priced in)
Analyst fair-value anchors well above market: consensus target ~272, third-party fair values ~314-328
risk_factors: The disruption might be real: Claude Design (Anthropic), Midjourney, Sora, and Canva attack casual/prosumer creative workflows with free or cheap generative tools - technological risk is High, not theoretical
ARR growth 10.2% is healthy but decelerating; pricing power erosion would show up here first
CEO transition adds execution uncertainty at the worst possible narrative moment

SBC data conflicted: one aggregator prints 1.94B as quarterly (implausible at ~30% of revenue vs Adobe's ~7% historical norm); treated as annual-scale and fully haircut from FCF - if SBC is genuinely ~7.8B/yr the value case collapses
Value-trap possibility: cheap software with a secular question mark is how ex-growth franchises (Teradata, Citrix) traded on the way down
